elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 高致病性禽流感 A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒最近从禽类 储存宿主 传播到美国奶牛中,引发了人们对哺乳动物适应和公共卫生风险的担忧。该研究旨在表征从威斯康星州奶牛群中新分离出的 H5N1 病毒,以了解其遗传和表型特性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究从 2025 年 12 月从威斯康星州奶牛群收集的散装牛奶中分离并鉴定了分支 2.3.4.4b、基因型 D1.1 H5N1 病毒(A/奶牛/威斯康星州/25G05743-001/2025)。
elements_zh.methods: 通过在含胚鸡蛋中盲传代来回收传染性病毒。确定了系统发育关系,并评估了该病毒的哺乳动物适应性取代和对小鼠的致病性。
elements_zh.main_results: 系统发育分析显示,WI5743-H5N1 与之前报道的内华达州和亚利桑那州奶牛中的 D1.1 病毒不同,表明可能是从当地鸟类来源独立引入的。该病毒编码了适应哺乳动物的 PB2-E627K 取代以及 HA、PB1-F2 和 NS1 中的其他氨基酸差异。在小鼠中,WI5743-H5N1 在呼吸组织中有效复制,在大脑中可检测到,并且表现出比最近的进化枝 2.3.4.4b(基因型 B3.13 病毒)更低的致死率。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证明了感染奶牛的 H5N1 病毒的遗传和表型多样性,并有独立 跨物种溢出 事件和哺乳动物适应 突变 的证据。该研究强调了预测新出现的 H5N1 病毒株的哺乳动物致病性的复杂性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调需要继续对奶牛中的 H5N1 病毒进行 监测 和功能表征,以便为潜在人畜共患 传播 的风险评估和防范提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它只关注单一菌株和小鼠模型,可能无法完全代表人类或牛的感染动态。由于样本量小且缺乏人体临床数据,证据强度中等。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have recently spilled over into U.S. dairy cattle from avian reservoirs, raising concerns about mammalian adaptation and public health risk. The study aimed to characterize a newly isolated H5N1 virus from a Wisconsin dairy herd to understand its genetic and phenotypic properties.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study isolated and characterized a clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype D1.1 H5N1 virus (A/dairy cow/Wisconsin/25G05743-001/2025) from bulk milk collected in December 2025 from a Wisconsin dairy herd identified through the National Milk Testing Strategy.
analysis_en.methods: Infectious virus was recovered by blind passage in embryonated chicken eggs. Phylogenetic relationships were determined, and the virus was assessed for mammalian-adapting substitutions and pathogenicity in mice.
analysis_en.main_results: Phylogenetic analysis showed WI5743-H5N1 is distinct from previously reported D1.1 viruses in dairy cattle from Nevada and Arizona, indicating an independent introduction likely from a local avian source. The virus encoded the mammalian-adapting PB2-E627K substitution and additional amino acid differences in HA, PB1-F2, and NS1. In mice, WI5743-H5N1 replicated efficiently in respiratory tissues, was detectable in the brain, and exhibited lower lethality than recent clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype B3.13 viruses.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate genetic and phenotypic diversity among H5N1 viruses infecting dairy cattle, with evidence of independent spillover events and mammalian-adapting mutations. The study highlights the complexity of predicting mammalian pathogenicity in emerging H5N1 strains.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the need for continued surveillance and functional characterization of H5N1 viruses in dairy cattle to inform risk assessment and preparedness for potential zoonotic transmission.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single isolate and mouse model, which may not fully represent human or bovine infection dynamics. The evidence strength is moderate due to the small sample size and absence of human clinical data.

title_zh: 威斯康星州奶牛中 2.3.4.4b 基因型 D1.1 H5N1 病毒的分离和表征
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) (HPAI H5N1) viruses of clade 2.3.4.4b have recently been detected in U.S. dairy cattle following multiple spillover events from avian reservoirs. In December 2025, HPAI H5N1 virus was identified in a dairy herd in Wisconsin through the National Milk Testing Strategy. Here, we report the isolation of a clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype D1.1 H5N1 virus, A/dairy cow/Wisconsin/25G05743-001/2025 (WI5743-H5N1), from bulk milk associated with the affected herd, describe its phylogenetic relationships, and assess its pathogenicity in mice. Infectious virus was recovered following blind passage in embryonated chicken eggs. Phylogenetic analysis demonstrated that WI5743-H5N1 is distinct from previously reported D1.1 viruses detected in dairy cattle in Nevada and Arizona, supporting an independent introduction into cattle, and indicating a likely local avian source. Compared with closely related avian viruses, WI5743-H5N1 encoded the mammalian-adapting substitution PB2-E627K and additional amino acid differences in HA, PB1-F2, and NS1. In mice, WI5743-H5N1 replicated efficiently in respiratory tissues and was detectable in the brain but exhibited lower lethality relative to other recent clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype B3.13 viruses. Together, these findings highlight the genetic and phenotypic diversity of HPAI H5N1 viruses infecting dairy cattle and underscore the importance of continued surveillance and functional characterization of emerging strains. IMPORTANCE Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses have recently entered U.S. dairy cattle through multiple spillover events from avian reservoirs, creating new opportunities for viral adaptation in mammals. Here, we describe the isolation and characterization of a clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype D1.1 H5N1 virus from bulk milk collected during a spillover event in Wisconsin in December 2025. Phylogenetic analyses demonstrated that this virus represents an independent introduction into dairy cattle distinct from previously reported D1.1 viruses identified in Nevada and Arizona. Although the virus encoded the mammalian-adapting PB2-E627K substitution, it exhibited comparatively low lethality in mice, highlighting the complexity of mammalian adaptation and pathogenicity in H5N1 viruses. These findings expand current understanding of the genetic and phenotypic diversity of H5N1 viruses infecting dairy cattle and emphasize the importance of continued surveillance and functional characterization of emerging strains.

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证明了感染奶牛的 H5N1 病毒的遗传和表型多样性,并有独立 跨物种溢出 事件和哺乳动物适应 突变 的证据。该研究强调了预测新出现的 H5N1 病毒株的哺乳动物致病性的复杂性。

title: PEGylated PolyaspartamideNanomicelle Delivery ofSelf-amplifying Avian Influenza mRNA Vaccine
abstract: Abstract The avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a major threat to the poultry industry and public health worldwide, highlighting the need for effective vaccines. Currently, the influenza vaccine for human use is an inactivated vaccine produced from eggs, which requires time-consuming and safe production processes. Messenger RNA (mRNA) is a transcriptional product of cells that can directly produce proteins, with no safety concerns regarding DNA template residues or integrated mutations in the genomic DNA. Recently, COVID-19 vaccines developed using mRNA to express the vaccine antigen have resulted in effective humoral and cellular immune responses. Additionally, mRNA can induce a robust cellular Toll-like receptor immune response and has the potential to serve as a promising vaccine adjuvant. In this study, we developed PEGylated polyamino polyplex nanomicelles encapsulating mRNA that expresses the AIV antigen. These nanomicelles were manufactured as an AIV vaccine, and their efficacy was evaluated in vivo. We produced a highly translation-effective, self-amplifying mRNA (saRNA) that expresses the main antigen, hemagglutinin (HA) protein of AIV. Subsequently, we encapsulated the HA-expressing saRNA in self-assembled polymeric nanomicelles using a PEGylated polyaspartamide block copolymer. Then, we compared the mRNA-loaded nanomicelle administration scenarios and the vaccine-elicited humoral (antibody titer and hemagglutination inhibition capability) and cellular immune responses (interferon-gamma [IFN-γ] and interleukin-4 [IL-4] cytokines) in mice. Our results demonstrated the successful development of an avian mRNA vaccine using polyamino self-assembled nanomicelles, which significantly enhanced both the humoral and cellular immune responses against the AIV antigen, providing a valuable reference for the further improvement of avian influenza mRNA vaccines in the future.

It highlights limitations of current inactivated egg-based vaccines and explores mRNA vaccine technology as a promising alternative.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research developed a self-amplifying mRNA vaccine expressing the hemagglutinin (HA) protein of AIV encapsulated in PEGylated polyaspartamide nanomicelles. The vaccine's efficacy was evaluated in vivo by comparing humoral and cellular immune responses in mice.

analysis.main_results: The results demonstrated that the avian mRNA vaccine using polyamino self-assembled nanomicelles significantly enhanced both humoral and cellular immune responses against the AIV antigen in mice.

title_zh: 聚乙二醇化聚天冬酰胺纳米胶束递送自扩增 禽流感 mRNA 疫苗
source_body_en: Abstract The avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a major threat to the poultry industry and public health worldwide, highlighting the need for effective vaccines. Currently, the influenza vaccine for human use is an inactivated vaccine produced from eggs, which requires time-consuming and safe production processes. Messenger RNA (mRNA) is a transcriptional product of cells that can directly produce proteins, with no safety concerns regarding DNA template residues or integrated mutations in the genomic DNA. Recently, COVID-19 vaccines developed using mRNA to express the vaccine antigen have resulted in effective humoral and cellular immune responses. Additionally, mRNA can induce a robust cellular Toll-like receptor immune response and has the potential to serve as a promising vaccine adjuvant. In this study, we developed PEGylated polyamino polyplex nanomicelles encapsulating mRNA that expresses the AIV antigen. These nanomicelles were manufactured as an AIV vaccine, and their efficacy was evaluated in vivo. We produced a highly translation-effective, self-amplifying mRNA (saRNA) that expresses the main antigen, hemagglutinin (HA) protein of AIV. Subsequently, we encapsulated the HA-expressing saRNA in self-assembled polymeric nanomicelles using a PEGylated polyaspartamide block copolymer. Then, we compared the mRNA-loaded nanomicelle administration scenarios and the vaccine-elicited humoral (antibody titer and hemagglutination inhibition capability) and cellular immune responses (interferon-gamma [IFN-γ] and interleukin-4 [IL-4] cytokines) in mice. Our results demonstrated the successful development of an avian mRNA vaccine using polyamino self-assembled nanomicelles, which significantly enhanced both the humoral and cellular immune responses against the AIV antigen, providing a valuable reference for the further improvement of avian influenza mRNA vaccines in the future.

title: Serovigilancia de influenza aviar H5N2 en patos y gansos domésticos de Río Blanco, San Marcos, Guatemala
abstract: Serological monitoring was conducted in domestic ducks and geese from the municipality of Río Blanco, San Marcos, in Guatemala’s western highlands. A total of 112 serum samples were taken from 83 Muscovy ducks (Cairina moschata) and 29 domestic geese (Anser anser var. domesticus) to determine the seroprevalence of H5N2 Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza (LPAI), by the haemagglutination inhibition test. A point seroprevalence of 0.89% was determined, with only 1 Muscovy duck out of 112 showing antibodies considered positive for the disease. The results indicate the presence of antibodies against H5N2 LPAI in a duck not vaccinated by the animal health service, suggesting exposure to the virus and possible circulation in the area. Therefore, it is necessary to remove obstacles to implement adequate surveillance and control strategies in the country.

source_body_en: Serological monitoring was conducted in domestic ducks and geese from the municipality of Río Blanco, San Marcos, in Guatemala’s western highlands. A total of 112 serum samples were taken from 83 Muscovy ducks (Cairina moschata) and 29 domestic geese (Anser anser var. domesticus) to determine the seroprevalence of H5N2 Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza (LPAI), by the haemagglutination inhibition test. The results indicate the presence of antibodies against H5N2 LPAI in a duck not vaccinated by the animal health service, suggesting exposure to the virus and possible circulation in the area. Therefore, it is necessary to remove obstacles to implement adequate surveillance and control strategies in the country.

title: Comparison of the adjuvant effect of AS01, AS03 and alum on the immune response to GMP-grade H5N1 antigen in guinea pigs
abstract: Abstract Adjuvants function as an enhancer and activator of the immune response and can be of pivotal importance for the efficacy of vaccines. AS01, which is a liposome formulation spiked with the saponin derivate QS-21 and the detoxified lipopolysaccharide MPL-A, and AS03, which is a squalene-based oil in water emulsion that contains antioxidant tocopherol, are modern, highly potent adjuvants that became integral to innovative vaccines. In the current study, guinea pigs –a well-established small animal model for human influenza-infections– were subcutaneously vaccinated with an influenza H5N1-antigen formulated with AS01, AS03, aluminium hydroxide or left unformulated. The induction of T- and B cells specific for the influenza antigen was assessed in dependence of the antigen formulation. H5N1-specific T cell responses were observed with all adjuvant formulations, but after six months were highest in the AS01- and AS03-immunized groups. The influenza specific antibody titres were highest in AS03-vaccinated guinea pigs. Importantly, AS03- and AS01-formulated influenza antigen also induced crossreactive antibodies inhibiting related H5N3- but not a distant H5N8-influenza strain. At the same time, it was observed that animals, which received the egg-produced H5N1 split antigen in combination with AS03, mounted xenoreactive, opsonizing antibodies that bound to chicken fibroblasts. No reactivity was observed to human fibroblasts. In summary, our results confirm the superior adjuvanticity of AS03 and of AS01 as compared to conventional alum or non-adjuvanted formulations. The presence of xenoreactive antibodies after AS03 vaccination was an unexpected observation. Further investigations will be required to appreciate the significance and identify the mechanisms of this findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared the adjuvant effect of AS01, AS03 and alum on the immune response to GMP-grade H5N1 antigen in guinea pigs, a well-established model for human influenza infections. The results showed that both AS01 and AS03 formulations induced stronger H5N1-specific T cell responses and higher antibody titres than alum or non-adjuvanted antigen after six months. Additionally, AS03 and AS01 formulations induced crossreactive antibodies against related H5N3 but not distant H5N8 strains. The study highlights the superior adjuvanticity of these formulations, which could inform vaccine development. However, the findings are based on an animal model and may not directly apply to humans. The evidence is strong within the context of the study but requires further investigation for broader implications.

abstract_zh: 摘要 佐剂作为 免疫应答 的增强剂和激活剂,对于 疫苗 的功效至关重要。AS01 是一种掺有皂苷衍生物 QS-21 和解毒脂多糖 MPL-A 的脂质体制剂,而 AS03 是一种基于角鲨烯的水包油乳液,含有抗氧化剂生育酚,它们是现代高效佐剂,成为创新型 疫苗 不可或缺的一部分。在当前的研究中,豚鼠(一种成熟的人类流感感染小动物模型)皮下接种了由 AS01、AS03、氢氧化铝配制或未配制的 H5N1 流感抗原。根据抗原制剂评估对流感抗原特异性的T细胞和B细胞的诱导。所有佐剂制剂均观察到 H5N1 特异性 T 细胞反应,但六个月后在 AS01 和 AS03 免疫组中反应最高。接种 AS03 的豚鼠的流感特异性抗体滴度最高。重要的是,AS03和AS01配制的流感抗原还诱导交叉反应抗体抑制相关的H5N3流感病毒株,但不抑制远处的H5N8流感病毒株。同时,观察到接受鸡蛋产生的 H5N1 裂解抗原与 AS03 组合的动物会产生与鸡成纤维细胞结合的异种反应性调理抗体。没有观察到对人成纤维细胞的反应性。总之,我们的结果证实了与传统明矾或无佐剂制剂相比,AS03 和 AS01 具有优异的佐剂性。AS03 疫苗接种 后异种反应抗体的存在是一个意想不到的观察结果。需要进一步的研究来理解这一发现的重要性并确定其机制。

analysis_zh.methods: 根据抗原配方评估对流感抗原特异性的 T 细胞和 B 细胞的诱导,并在接种疫苗的动物中测量 免疫应答。
analysis_zh.main_results: 所有佐剂制剂均观察到 H5N1 特异性 T 细胞反应,但六个月后,AS01 和 AS03 免疫组的反应最高。在接种 AS03 的豚鼠中,流感特异性抗体滴度也最高。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果证实了 AS03 和 AS01 与传统明矾或无佐剂制剂相比具有优异的佐剂性,凸显了它们在 疫苗 开发中的潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,AS01 和 AS03 可能是提高 疫苗 对 H5N1 的疗效的有价值的佐剂,这对开发更有效的流感 疫苗 具有重要意义。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于豚鼠作为动物模型,证据基于在该模型中观察到的 免疫应答,这可能无法完全转化为人类结果。

title: Host cell entry receptors as pharmacological targets in respiratory viral infections: from biology to clinical translation
abstract: Respiratory viral infections caused by seasonal influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and pandemic-potential coronaviruses are responsible for several million hospitalisations and an estimated several hundred thousand deaths each year, a burden underscored by the severe 2024–2025 influenza season and the continued emergence of zoonotic threats such as clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1. This review critically examines the pharmacological basis for targeting host cell-surface receptors as a strategy for the treatment and prophylaxis of respiratory viral infections, evaluates the current evidence for each major receptor axis, and identifies the key translational gaps that must be addressed. Respiratory viruses, including influenza, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV, collectively cause millions of hospitalisations annually, and the persistent challenges of antigenic drift, zoonotic emergence, and antiviral resistance highlight the need for mechanistically distinct strategies. Host-directed therapies (HDTs) targeting conserved receptors (ACE2, DPP4, sialic acids, TMPRSS2) exploit genetically stable host factors required for viral entry. Across the receptor axes reviewed here, we appraise more than a dozen candidate agents spanning preclinical development through Phase III evaluation, including TMPRSS2 inhibitors, soluble ACE2 decoys, anti-CD147 and receptor-blocking monoclonal antibodies, the sialidase fusion protein DAS181, and avian IgY preparations. This evidence reveals a consistent gap between robust preclinical activity and as-yet-limited clinical efficacy. We conclude that host receptor targeting is a mechanistically rational but still clinically unproven component of the respiratory antiviral landscape; its value is most plausibly realised in defined niches—prophylaxis, early outpatient treatment, and combination with direct-acting antivirals—and within pandemic preparedness frameworks, provided that the safety, delivery, and trial-design challenges identified here are resolved.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines pharmacological targeting of host cell-surface receptors as a strategy for treating and preventing respiratory viral infections, focusing on avian influenza A viruses (e.g., H5N1, H5N6, H7N9) and other zoonotic respiratory pathogens. The central question addresses the translational potential of host-directed therapies (HDTs) targeting conserved receptors such as ACE2, DPP4, sialic acids, and TMPRSS2 for avian influenza and related zoonotic threats.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis that critically evaluates the pharmacological basis for targeting host cell receptors in respiratory viral infections, appraising candidate agents across preclinical and clinical stages. It identifies translational gaps but does not report systematic search dates, eligibility criteria, or included-study counts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that host receptor targeting is mechanistically rational but remains clinically unproven for respiratory viral infections. It highlights a consistent gap between robust preclinical activity and limited clinical efficacy across receptor axes, including TMPRSS2 inhibitors, soluble ACE2 decoys, anti-CD147 antibodies, and sialidase fusion proteins.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies unresolved challenges in translating preclinical efficacy to clinical outcomes, including safety concerns, delivery barriers, and trial-design limitations. It notes that while HDTs target conserved host factors, their clinical value remains unproven, particularly in pandemic preparedness frameworks.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes resolving safety, delivery, and trial-design challenges to realize the potential of host receptor targeting in prophylaxis, early outpatient treatment, and combination with direct-acting antivirals. It emphasizes the need for pandemic preparedness frameworks to integrate HDTs, contingent on addressing identified translational gaps.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates host cell receptor targeting as a strategy for treating and preventing respiratory viral infections, with a focus on avian influenza A viruses and zoonotic threats. It synthesizes evidence on host-directed therapies (HDTs) targeting conserved receptors such as ACE2, DPP4, sialic acids, and TMPRSS2, including TMPRSS2 inhibitors, soluble ACE2 decoys, anti-CD147 antibodies, and sialidase fusion proteins. The review concludes that while HDTs are mechanistically rational, their clinical efficacy remains unproven, with a consistent gap between preclinical promise and limited real-world success. Key challenges include safety, delivery barriers, and trial-design limitations. The authors prioritize addressing these translational gaps to enable HDTs in prophylaxis, early outpatient treatment, and combination therapies, particularly within pandemic preparedness frameworks.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了 宿主 细胞表面受体的药理学靶向作为治疗和预防呼吸道病毒感染的策略,重点关注 禽流感 A 病毒(例如 H5N1、H5N6、H7N9)和其他人畜共患呼吸道病原体。核心问题涉及针对 宿主 和相关人畜共患威胁的保守受体(如 ACE2、DPP4、唾液酸和 TMPRSS2)的 宿主 定向疗法 (HDT) 的转化潜力。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇叙述性综合文章,批判性地评估了针对呼吸道病毒感染中 宿主 细胞受体的药理学基础,评估了临床前和临床阶段的候选药物。它确定了翻译差距,但不报告系统检索日期、资格标准或纳入研究计数。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,宿主 受体靶向在机制上是合理的,但在呼吸道病毒感染方面尚未得到临床证实。它强调了跨受体轴(包括 TMPRSS2 抑制剂、可溶性 ACE2 诱饵、抗 CD147 抗体和唾液酸酶融合蛋白)的强大临床前活性和有限的临床疗效之间的一致差距。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了将临床前疗效转化为临床结果方面尚未解决的挑战,包括安全性问题、交付障碍和试验设计限制。它指出,虽然 HDT 以保守的 宿主 因子为目标,但其临床价值尚未得到证实,特别是在大流行防范框架中。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查优先考虑解决安全性、交付和试验设计挑战,以实现 宿主 受体靶向在预防、早期门诊 治疗 以及与直接作用 抗病毒药物 组合方面的潜力。它强调大流行病防范框架需要整合 HDT,这取决于解决已确定的转化差距。

abstract_zh: 由季节性流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和潜在大流行的冠状病毒引起的呼吸道病毒感染每年导致数百万人住院,估计有数十万人死亡,2024-2025 年严重的流感季节和人畜共患威胁(如进化枝 2.3.4.4b H5N1)的持续出现加剧了这一负担。本综述批判性地研究了靶向 宿主 细胞表面受体作为 治疗 和预防呼吸道病毒感染的策略的药理学基础,评估了每个主要受体轴的当前证据,并确定了必须解决的关键翻译差距。呼吸道病毒,包括流感、RSV、SARS-CoV-2 和 MERS-CoV,每年总共导致数百万人住院,抗原漂移、人畜共患疾病的出现和 抗病毒药物 耐药性等持续挑战突出表明需要采取机制上不同的策略。针对保守受体(ACE2、DPP4、唾液酸、TMPRSS2)的 宿主 定向疗法 (HDT) 利用病毒进入所需的遗传稳定的 宿主 因子。在此回顾的受体轴中,我们评估了十多种从临床前开发到 III 期评估的候选药物,包括 TMPRSS2 抑制剂、可溶性 ACE2 诱饵、抗 CD147 和受体阻断单克隆抗体、唾液酸酶融合蛋白 DAS181 和禽类 IgY 制剂。这一证据揭示了强大的临床前活性与迄今为止有限的临床疗效之间的一致差距。我们得出的结论是,宿主 受体靶向是呼吸 抗病毒药物 景观中机械合理但尚未得到临床证实的组成部分;它的价值最有可能在特定的领域(预防、早期门诊 治疗 以及与直接作用的 抗病毒药物 组合)以及大流行防范框架内实现,前提是此处确定的安全性、交付和试验设计挑战得到解决。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇叙述性综合文章,批判性地评估了针对呼吸道病毒感染中 宿主 细胞受体的药理学基础,评估了临床前和临床阶段的候选药物。它确定了翻译差距,但不报告系统检索日期、资格标准或纳入研究计数。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,宿主 受体靶向在机制上是合理的,但在呼吸道病毒感染方面尚未得到临床证实。它强调了跨受体轴(包括 TMPRSS2 抑制剂、可溶性 ACE2 诱饵、抗 CD147 抗体和唾液酸酶融合蛋白)的强大临床前活性和有限的临床疗效之间的一致差距。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了将临床前疗效转化为临床结果方面尚未解决的挑战,包括安全性问题、交付障碍和试验设计限制。它指出,虽然 HDT 以保守的 宿主 因子为目标,但其临床价值尚未得到证实,特别是在大流行防范框架中。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查优先考虑解决安全性、交付和试验设计挑战,以实现 宿主 受体靶向在预防、早期门诊 治疗 以及与直接作用 抗病毒药物 组合方面的潜力。它强调大流行病防范框架需要整合 HDT,这取决于解决已确定的转化差距。

title: Conserved influenza A epitope candidate regions and a benchmark of ESM-2 sequence features
abstract: Influenza A virus antigenic drift forces annual vaccine reformulation, motivating the search for conserved epitope candidates that could support broadly protective vaccines. We systematically screened influenza A virus sequences (H1N1, H3N2, H5N1; nine viral proteins) to define 98 conserved candidate regions, 38 of which were identical across the H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1 consensus sequences, all in the polymerase complex and nucleoprotein (PB2, PB1, PA, NP), whereas the ten surface-glycoprotein (HA/NA) candidates were subtype-specific. We then benchmarked two protein-language-model (ESM-2) features against alignment conservation. Group-masked log-probability correlated moderately with MSA conservation (Spearman rho = 0.25 to 0.39 for HA) but provided no incremental value for T-cell epitope discrimination (change in AUROC +0.004, p = 0.46); attention-derived contact-density was not a valid solvent-accessibility proxy. A curated antibody-epitope benchmark (22 clusters, 5 neutralization-supported) was underpowered for a high-confidence B-cell test. We document data-quality and reproducibility pitfalls (length heterogeneity, coordinate mapping, and pseudoreplication) and release the auditable benchmark. These results provide an auditable candidate resource and show that, in the evaluated benchmarks, ESM-2 sequence scores did not improve epitope prioritization beyond alignment-derived conservation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify conserved epitope candidates in influenza A viruses to support the development of broadly protective vaccines, as antigenic drift necessitates annual vaccine reformulation. The researchers systematically analyzed sequences from H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1 subtypes across nine viral proteins, identifying 98 conserved regions. They benchmarked ESM-2 features against alignment conservation, finding that group-masked log-probability correlated moderately with MSA conservation but did not improve T-cell epitope discrimination. Attention-derived contact-density was not a valid solvent-accessibility proxy. The study concluded that ESM-2 sequence scores did not enhance epitope prioritization beyond traditional alignment methods. It also highlighted data-quality and reproducibility challenges, such as length heterogeneity and pseudoreplication, and noted that the antibody-epitope benchmark was underpowered for high-confidence B-cell testing. These findings provide an auditable resource for epitope candidates and underscore the need for further research into alternative methods for epitope prioritization.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在鉴定甲型流感病毒中的保守候选表位,以支持广泛保护性 疫苗 的开发,因为抗原漂移需要每年重新配制 疫苗。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及对多种亚型和蛋白质的甲型流感病毒序列进行系统筛选,重点关注聚合酶复合物和核蛋白内的保守区域。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用群体屏蔽对数概率和注意力衍生接触密度作为指标,对 ESM-2 序列特征与比对保守进行基准测试。
elements_zh.main_results: 组屏蔽对数概率与 MSA 保守性显示出中等相关性,但没有改善 T 细胞表位辨别力,而注意力衍生的接触密度并不是有效的溶剂可及性代理。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在评估的基准中,ESM-2 序列评分并未增强表位优先级,超越传统的比对衍生保护方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果为候选表位提供了可审核的资源,并强调了使用 ESM-2 特征对甲型流感病毒进行表位优先排序的局限性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究指出了数据质量和重现性问题,例如长度异质性和假复制,并承认抗体表位基准对于高置信度 B 细胞测试来说动力不足。

abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒抗原漂移迫使每年重新配制 疫苗,从而激发了对可支持广泛保护性 疫苗 的保守候选表位的搜索。我们系统地筛选了甲型流感病毒序列(H1N1、H3N2、H5N1;九种病毒蛋白),以确定 98 个保守候选区域,其中 38 个在 H1N1、H3N2 和 H5N1 共有序列中是相同的,全部位于聚合酶复合物和核蛋白(PB2、PB1、PA、NP)中,而 10 个表面糖蛋白(HA/NA)候选区域是亚型特异性的。然后,我们对两个蛋白质语言模型 (ESM-2) 特征与对齐保守性进行了基准测试。组屏蔽对数概率与 MSA 保守性适度相关(对于 HA,Spearman rho = 0.25 至 0.39),但没有为 T 细胞表位辨别提供增量值(AUROC 变化 +0.004,p = 0.46);注意力衍生的接触密度并不是有效的溶剂可及性代理。精心设计的抗体表位基准(22 个簇,5 个支持中和)对于高置信度 B 细胞测试来说动力不足。我们记录数据质量和可重复性缺陷(长度异质性、坐标映射和伪复制)并发布可审核的基准。这些结果提供了可审核的候选资源,并表明,在评估的基准中,ESM-2 序列评分并没有改善除比对衍生的保护之外的表位优先顺序。

title: NZ has spent years preparing for H5N1 bird flu. For some species, it may not be enough

full_text: The arrival of the highly pathogenic H5N1 strain of bird flu in Aotearoa New Zealand last month triggered a national response years in the making. By then, surveillance systems, species protection plans and even vaccines for some birds were already in place as part of a coordinated approach led by the Ministry for Primary Industries. Yet even these preparations may not be enough to save some of the country’s rarest birds. Many survive in tiny, isolated populations with limited genetic diversity. For these highly vulnerable species, the outcome may depend not only on conservation efforts, but also on chance. Genetic diversity acts as nature’s insurance policy against disease. In large populations, some individuals are more likely to survive an outbreak and help the population recover. But in small, isolated populations with little genetic diversity, those odds are much lower, leaving species far more vulnerable to extinction. Why vaccines can only do so much H5N1 has caused mass mortality events in wild birds around the world since emerging in 2020, making it one of the most significant disease threats many species have faced in decades. Vaccines offer one important layer of protection, but they are no silver bullet. A Department of Conservation-led vaccine trial involving five intensively managed threatened species found that effective protection requires at least two doses administered a few weeks apart. In kakī – the critically endangered black stilt and one of the world’s rarest wading birds – immunity declined after three months, meaning a third dose will be needed. With the trial now complete and H5N1 in New Zealand, vaccinations are underway, beginning with 300 individuals from the five species involved in the study. The greater challenge, however, is delivering that protection in the wild. Catching a threatened bird once can be difficult. Catching the same bird again, at exactly the right time for a second or third dose, can be harder still. Vaccinate too early and immunity may wane before the virus arrives. Vaccinate too late and the opportunity may be missed. These practical constraints mean conservation teams cannot simply vaccinate every bird. Instead, they must make difficult decisions about where limited time and resources will have the greatest impact. On Rēkohu/Wharekauri/Chatham Islands, for example, plans are underway to vaccinate several of its threatened species, including black robin (karure, kakaruia). The species’ small population on Maung’ Rē/Mangere may make it possible to vaccinate every individual with two doses. On nearby Hokoreoreoro/Rangatira, however, the larger population is likely to require a different approach, with efforts focused on vaccinating as many birds as can be reliably caught and recaptured while balancing the needs of other species. The harsh reality is that some birds will receive the right protection at the right time, but others will not. Different birds, different risks Just as importantly, not all species face the same level of risk from H5N1. It varies depending on where those species live and how they behave. For colonial nesting species such as many seabirds, breeding creates the ideal conditions for the virus to spread, as birds gather closely in large numbers. For solitary nesters such as kakī, however, breeding is one of the safer times of year because individuals are more widely dispersed. Their risk increases outside the breeding season, when they congregate at estuaries alongside other bird species. If bird flu does push some species even closer to extinction, it will not be for lack of effort. Across the country, dedicated teams will be working tirelessly to protect the country’s most vulnerable wildlife. To date, the incursion remains limited. Two wild birds in the Wellington region have tested positive for H5N1, with no further detections since mid-July and no evidence of widespread mortality in wildlife or spread into poultry. But overseas experience has shown how quickly the situation can change, making continued surveillance and preparedness essential. Recent media coverage of an injured ruru (morepork) offered a glimpse of how difficult and emotional those decisions can be. In the months and years ahead, conservation staff will need not only the best available science, but also patience, understanding and kindness from the communities they serve. For now, H5N1 is the immediate threat. It is unlikely to be the last. As emerging diseases become an increasingly important conservation challenge, building resilient species and ecosystems will be just as important as responding to each new outbreak. If you find a single sick, injured or dead native bird, contact the Department of Conservation (0800 362 468). If you find three or more sick or dead birds together, report it immediately to the Ministry for Primary Industries (0800 80 99 66).

title_original: NZ has spent years preparing for H5N1 bird flu. For some species, it may not be enough

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study examines why New Zealand’s existing H5N1 preparedness may be insufficient for its most vulnerable bird species despite years of national planning and surveillance systems.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The analysis synthesizes national surveillance systems, conservation plans, and vaccine trials led by the Ministry for Primary Industries and Department of Conservation, focusing on threatened bird species with limited genetic diversity.
analysis.methods: The paper reviews vaccine trial protocols for five intensively managed threatened species, including dosing schedules and immunity duration, and evaluates practical constraints in delivering multi-dose vaccination in wild populations.
analysis.main_results: Vaccine effectiveness requires at least two doses, with immunity declining after three months in kakī, necessitating a third dose. Practical challenges include the difficulty of recapturing birds for subsequent doses and balancing limited resources across species and locations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors highlight that while vaccines provide critical protection, their real-world application is constrained by logistical challenges and species-specific risks, underscoring the need for targeted conservation strategies rather than blanket vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize prioritizing vaccination efforts for species with feasible recapture rates and focusing on high-risk periods, such as colonial nesting seasons, to mitigate H5N1 impacts on New Zealand’s rarest birds.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is observational and based on a single vaccine trial with five species, lacking broader population-level data or randomized comparisons, which limits generalizability and strength of inference.

analysis.summary_en: New Zealand’s H5N1 preparedness includes surveillance systems, species protection plans, and vaccines for some birds, yet these measures may not suffice for its most vulnerable species. Small, isolated populations with limited genetic diversity face heightened extinction risk, as immunity from vaccines wanes without repeated doses. A Department of Conservation-led trial found that effective protection requires at least two doses, with kakī needing a third dose after three months due to declining immunity. Practical constraints, such as the difficulty of recapturing birds for subsequent doses, further complicate vaccination efforts. Conservation teams must prioritize species and locations where vaccination is feasible, such as the black robin on Maung’ Rē/Mangere, while balancing resources across other threatened species. Risk varies by species behavior, with colonial nesters facing higher transmission risks during breeding seasons. While H5N1 detections remain limited in New Zealand, overseas experience underscores the need for continued surveillance and adaptive conservation strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了为什么新西兰现有的 H5N1 防备措施可能不足以应对其最脆弱的鸟类物种,尽管进行了多年的国家规划和 监测 系统。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该分析综合了由第一产业部和保护部领导的国家 监测 系统、保护计划和 疫苗 试验,重点关注遗传多样性有限的受威胁鸟类物种。
elements_zh.methods: 该论文回顾了针对五种集中管理的受威胁物种的 疫苗 试验方案,包括给药时间表和免疫持续时间,并评估了在野生种群中提供多剂量 疫苗接种 的实际限制。
elements_zh.main_results: 疫苗 的有效性需要至少两剂,服用 kakī 三个月后免疫力下降,需要第三剂。实际挑战包括重新捕获鸟类以进行后续剂量的困难以及平衡跨物种和地点的有限资源的困难。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者强调,虽然 疫苗 提供了关键的保护,但它们在现实世界中的应用受到后勤挑战和物种特定风险的限制,强调需要有针对性的保护策略,而不是一揽子 疫苗接种。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调,疫苗接种 工作应优先考虑具有可行重新捕获率的物种,并重点关注高风险时期,例如殖民地筑巢季节,以减轻 H5N1 对新西兰最稀有鸟类的影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据是观察性的,基于对五个物种的单一 疫苗 试验,缺乏更广泛的群体水平数据或随机比较,这限制了推论的普遍性和强度。

Liz Brown, CC BY-NC-ND NZ has spent years preparing for H5N1 bird flu. For some species, it may not be enough Published: August 17, 2026 3:17pm EDT The arrival of the highly pathogenic H5N1 strain of bird flu in Aotearoa New Zealand last month triggered a national response years in the making. By then, surveillance systems, species protection plans and even vaccines for some birds were already in place as part of a coordinated approach led by the Ministry for Primary Industries. Yet even these preparations may not be enough to save some of the country’s rarest birds. Many survive in tiny, isolated populations with limited genetic diversity. For these highly vulnerable species, the outcome may depend not only on conservation efforts, but also on chance. Genetic diversity acts as nature’s insurance policy against disease. In large populations, some individuals are more likely to survive an outbreak and help the population recover. But in small, isolated populations with little genetic diversity, those odds are much lower, leaving species far more vulnerable to extinction. Why vaccines can only do so much H5N1 has caused mass mortality events in wild birds around the world since emerging in 2020, making it one of the most significant disease threats many species have faced in decades. Vaccines offer one important layer of protection, but they are no silver bullet. A Department of Conservation-led vaccine trial involving five intensively managed threatened species found that effective protection requires at least two doses administered a few weeks apart. In kakī – the critically endangered black stilt and one of the world’s rarest wading birds – immunity declined after three months, meaning a third dose will be needed. With the trial now complete and H5N1 in New Zealand, vaccinations are underway, beginning with 300 individuals from the five species involved in the study. The greater challenge, however, is delivering that protection in the wild. Catching a threatened bird once can be difficult. Catching the same bird again, at exactly the right time for a second or third dose, can be harder still. Vaccinate too early and immunity may wane before the virus arrives. Vaccinate too late and the opportunity may be missed. These practical constraints mean conservation teams cannot simply vaccinate every bird. Instead, they must make difficult decisions about where limited time and resources will have the greatest impact. On Rēkohu/Wharekauri/Chatham Islands, for example, plans are underway to vaccinate several of its threatened species, including black robin (karure, kakaruia). The black robin (karure, kakaruia) endemic to the Chatham Islands, lying to the east of New Zealand. Robin Bush/Getty Images The species’ small population on Maung’ Rē/Mangere may make it possible to vaccinate every individual with two doses. On nearby Hokoreoreoro/Rangatira, however, the larger population is likely to require a different approach, with efforts focused on vaccinating as many birds as can be reliably caught and recaptured while balancing the needs of other species. The harsh reality is that some birds will receive the right protection at the right time, but others will not. Different birds, different risks Just as importantly, not all species face the same level of risk from H5N1. It varies depending on where those species live and how they behave. For colonial nesting species such as many seabirds, breeding creates the ideal conditions for the virus to spread, as birds gather closely in large numbers. For solitary nesters such as kakī, however, breeding is one of the safer times of year because individuals are more widely dispersed. Their risk increases outside the breeding season, when they congregate at estuaries alongside other bird species. If bird flu does push some species even closer to extinction, it will not be for lack of effort. Across the country, dedicated teams will be working tirelessly to protect the country’s most vulnerable wildlife. To date, the incursion remains limited. Two wild birds in the Wellington region have tested positive for H5N1, with no further detections since mid-July and no evidence of widespread mortality in wildlife or spread into poultry. But overseas experience has shown how quickly the situation can change, making continued surveillance and preparedness essential. Recent media coverage of an injured ruru (morepork) offered a glimpse of how difficult and emotional those decisions can be. In the months and years ahead, conservation staff will need not only the best available science, but also patience, understanding and kindness from the communities they serve. For now, H5N1 is the immediate threat. It is unlikely to be the last. As emerging diseases become an increasingly important conservation challenge, building resilient species and ecosystems will be just as important as responding to each new outbreak. If you find a single sick, injured or dead native bird, contact the Department of Conservation (0800 362 468). If you find three or more sick or dead birds together, report it immediately to the Ministry for Primary Industries (0800 80 99 66). title: Newton Divided Difference Optimization for Fingerprint-Based Neural Virtual Screening against Avian Influenza A/H9N2
abstract: Avian influenza A/H9N2 poses persistent zoonotic and veterinary threats, yet efficient computational tools for antiviral compound prioritization remain underdeveloped, particularly with respect to optimizer behavior in high-dimensional neural screening. This study proposes Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization, a lightweight positive diagonal curvature-aware training strategy, as a novel optimizer for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2, with the objective of evaluating its performance across aligned molecular fingerprint representations and chemically structured validation protocols. An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments. A fixed multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier was trained with NDD and seven baseline optimizers under stratified, scaffold-key, and similarity-cluster split protocols across five repeated seeds. NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteriztic – Area Under the Curve) and PR-AUC (Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve) on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872. Architecture-sensitivity tests confirmed stable NDD performance across multiple network configurations, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.9876 to 0.9890. Compared with Hessian-free optimization, NDD reduced per-run runtime from approximately 50–54 seconds to approximately 8 seconds on Klekota–Roth under the same CPU-only configuration while achieving comparable ranking performance. The novelty of this work lies in the first systematic assessment of NDD for H9N2 neural virtual screening, demonstrating that positive diagonal curvature-aware scaling provides a practical, stable, and computationally efficient optimization alternative in sparse high-dimensional ligand-based screening settings, although external validation and prospective experimental confirmation remain necessary before practical antiviral prioritization.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization as a novel approach for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2. The researchers evaluated NDD's performance using a benchmark of 1,459 molecules represented by different molecular fingerprints and trained a multilayer perceptron classifier under various split protocols. NDD achieved the highest ROC-AUC and PR-AUC on Klekota–Roth fingerprints and significantly reduced runtime compared to Hessian-free optimization. The study demonstrates that NDD provides a computationally efficient and stable alternative for antiviral compound prioritization, though external validation is needed before practical application.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 禽流感 A/H9N2 造成持续的人畜共患病和兽医威胁,但用于 抗病毒药物 化合物优先级排序的有效计算工具仍然不发达,特别是在高维神经筛选中的​​优化器行为方面。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究提出牛顿差分(NDD)优化作为一种​​针对 禽流感 A/H9N2 的基于指纹的神经虚拟筛选的新型优化器,目的是评估其在对齐的分子指纹表示和化学结构验证协议中的性能。
elements_zh.methods: 由 615 种候选活性化合物和 844 种诱饵组成的 1,459 个分子的对齐基准由 EState(79 个特征)、PubChem(881 个特征)和 Klekota–Roth(4,860 个特征)指纹代表,共享相同的分子身份、标签和分割分配。固定多层感知器 (MLP) 分类器使用 NDD 和七个基线优化器在分层、支架键和相似性聚类分割协议下跨五个重复种子进行训练。
elements_zh.main_results: NDD 在支架关键和相似性聚类协议下在 Klekota–Roth 指纹上实现了最高的描述性 ROC-AUC 和 PR-AUC,并且在分层分割下保持竞争力,ROC-AUC 为 0.9872。架构敏感性测试证实了跨多种网络配置的稳定 NDD 性能,ROC-AUC 值范围为 0.9876 至 0.9890。与无 Hessian 优化相比,在相同的仅 CPU 配置下,NDD 将 Klekota-Roth 上的每次运行时间从大约 50-54 秒减少到大约 8 秒,同时实现了相当的排名性能。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这项工作的新颖性在于首次对 H9N2 神经虚拟筛选的 NDD 进行系统评估,证明正对角线曲率感知缩放在基于稀疏高维配体的筛选设置中提供了实用、稳定且计算高效的优化替代方案。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为针对 禽流感 A/H9N2 的 抗病毒药物 化合物优先排序提供了一种计算有效的优化策略,这可以加速针对这种人畜共患威胁的潜在治疗方法的发现。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在实施实际的 抗病毒药物 优先级排序之前,外部验证和前瞻性实验确认仍然是必要的。由于研究的计算性质和实验验证的需要,证据强度中等。

title: Why Not Antivirals? Reconsidering Influenza Treatment in Children
abstract: In this issue of Pediatrics, Huang et al1 shed important light on the association between antiviral use and reduced influenza-related hospitalizations in children. Using a large national health care database from Taiwan and accounting for a number of clinically relevant factors, the case-control study decisively showed that early antiviral use within 48 hours of symptoms onset was associated with an 81% reduction in the risk of influenza-related hospitalization. Rigorous sensitivity analyses challenging study assumptions did not alter their conclusions. These findings closely resemble several other well performed observational studies powered to assess the outcome of influenza hospitalization and antiviral use.2–12 These studies varied in their definition of influenza-related or any cause hospitalization and whether antivirals were used early or late. Several of these studies also controlled for vaccination status, duration of symptoms, and health care use and assessed negative controls for residual biases. Performed over different influenza seasons in various countries using different methods and data sources, they clearly demonstrate clinically impactful reductions in hospitalization and influenza-related complications with antiviral use.Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are the gold standard study design for assessing therapeutic effectiveness, but they have limitations, particularly when the study outcome is an uncommon event, such as influenza-related hospitalization. In contrast, observational studies use much larger data from real-world settings to provide an adequate sample size to evaluate uncommon occurrences. When rigorously conducted, observational studies can provide important evidence when RCTs cannot.13,14 In fact, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) recently stressed the power of observational studies, stating that nonrandomized data can lead to “actionable causal conclusions.”15 The Huang study published this month in Pediatrics, put in the context of other studies in outpatients (Figure 1), provides “actionable causal conclusions” that early antiviral treatment shortly after symptom onset decreases influenza-associated hospitalizations and associated complications.Despite repeated studies showing the clinical benefit of antiviral treatment in outpatients on hospitalization, why are they not used more? It is likely because of the controversy that has surrounded the association between antiviral use and reduced hospitalizations for almost 2 decades. This is largely because RCTs are underpowered to assess a hospitalization outcome.16–18 RCTs for influenza antivirals were performed to assess minor endpoints in outpatients with uncomplicated influenza, such as time to alleviation of symptoms, and were not designed to evaluate serious or uncommon outcomes. The antiviral oseltamivir was approved in 1999 based on 2 RCTs conducted in previously healthy adolescents and adults with laboratory-confirmed influenza.19,20 Patients treated within 48 hours of symptom onset randomized to oseltamivir had a 1.3 days reduction of illness when compared with placebo recipients.19,20 In 2003, several clinical trials were combined in a publication in Arch Intern Med demonstrating that oseltamivir treatment reduced all-cause hospitalization by 59% (P = 0.02) and lower respiratory tract infections treated with antibiotics by 55% (P = <0.001).21 In 2006, the Cochrane group published a meta-analysis of RCTs concluding a 68% reduction in pneumonia with oseltamivir treatment of influenza.22 However, this publication triggered widespread controversy, later suggesting that clinical trial data had been withheld by Roche (the manufacturer of oseltamivir) and that the oseltamivir benefit for reducing influenza-related hospitalization had been oversold.Additional trial data were eventually provided by Roche and another Cochrane review published in 2014 found that oseltamivir treatment of outpatients with influenza reduced pneumonia by 55% but did not reduce any cause hospitalization.23 Importantly, the Cochrane review analyzed the risk of hospitalization in the influenza-like illness population (rather than the laboratory-confirmed influenza population). In their primary analysis of oseltamivir and hospitalization, 33% of participants included did not have influenza, likely biasing results toward the null. The same Cochrane review also reported that oseltamivir treatment reduced the duration of influenza symptoms in children by 29 hours, a clinically meaningful reduction, similar to subsequent meta-analyses in children24 and data provided to support FDA approval. Yet, this Cochrane review led many to conclude that oseltamivir had minimal or no impact on hospitalizations.To address this controversy surrounding oseltamivir’s effect on pneumonia and hospitalization, the Multiparty Group for Advice on Science assembled a research team25 and obtained an unrestricted grant from Roche to perform an additional meta-analysis that included more completed trial information and individual patient data rather than aggregated results, the preferred analytic method for meta-analyses.26,27 This meta-analysis of oseltamivir treatment in outpatient adults with laboratory-confirmed uncomplicated influenza published by Dobson et al in the Lancet25 reported reductions in both hospitalization by 63% and pneumonia by 44%.25,27Several subsequent meta-analyses reported mixed findings for influenza antivirals and influenza-related hospitalization using clinical trial data.18,24,28,29 However, there were significant limitations to these studies. Outpatient RCTs of antivirals were not designed to evaluate severe outcomes such as influenza complications or hospitalization. In fact, pivotal clinical trials that led to FDA approval of oseltamivir did not include hospitalization as a primary or sometimes even a tertiary outcome. In clinical trials, especially older trials, nonprimary end points may be less precisely chosen, measured, analyzed, and reported compared with primary end points. Meta-analysis of RCTs in both children and adults are severely underpowered to evaluate hospitalization as an outcome.18,24 For example, a recent meta-analysis in JAMA Internal Medicine, one of the largest to date, included 6166 individuals, 3324 of whom received oseltamivir. The study concluded there was no reduction in any-cause hospitalization with oseltamivir (risk ratio [RR] 0.77; 95% CI 0.47–1.27). However, another valid interpretation would be that the study was substantially underpowered to determine a precise effect estimate and that oseltamivir may indeed reduce hospitalization.16,17 One of us (JA) recently reported that if the true RR for oseltamivir treated relative to untreated patients was 0.77 (a 23% reduction), a prospective trial would need approximately 87 000 participants (48 704 oseltamivir exposed and 38 963 unexposed) to reject the null hypothesis.16,17 Simply put, the question of “Does oseltamivir reduce hospitalization?” cannot be properly answered with pooled data from RCTs of oseltamivir treatment in outpatients conducted to date and must be assessed in observational studies, such as the Huang study in this issue of Pediatrics.It is biologically plausible that early use of influenza antivirals can reduce hospitalization for influenza-related illnesses because they reduce viral load and viral-mediated inflammation.30–32 RCTs and well-designed observational studies have also shown that antivirals reduce influenza complications such as pneumonia, otitis media, sinusitis, and neurologic events in children and adolescents.2,12,24,25,33 The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimates that current antiviral prescribing practices prevent up to 14 184 hospitalizations per season and that a 50% improvement in access, testing, and prescribing could avert over 71 000 hospitalizations.34For nearly 20 years, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), CDC, and the Infectious Disease Society of America (IDSA) have recommended prompt antiviral treatment in all high-risk children with influenza and consideration of use in those within 48 hours of symptom onset.35–37 However, despite these recommendations, pediatric providers remain very hesitant to prescribe antivirals and at the same time overprescribe antibiotics. Approximately 40% of high-risk children with influenza do not receive a recommended antiviral, a trend that has worsened since the COVID-19 pandemic.38,39 Recent findings published in Pediatrics40,41 on reasons for the underprescribing of antivirals for influenza are shockingly similar to results from a study conducted 15 years ago by the CDC42 and include the following: 1) lack of awareness of national guidelines, 2) questions about the effectiveness of antivirals, and 3) concern about adverse events associated with antivirals, particularly vomiting and neuropsychiatric events.Although we have addressed the first 2 of these issues, we would like to conclude this commentary discussing the safety of oseltamivir. Although over 2 decades of clinical studies support the safety of influenza antivirals, many providers remain very concerned about antiviral-related vomiting and neuropsychiatric events. However, vomiting is not a common adverse event with oseltamivir. Oseltamivir RCTs in children demonstrate a 5.8% increase in vomiting compared with placebo.24 This means that for every 17 patients treated with oseltamivir, 1 will experience additional vomiting. Oseltamivir-related nausea and vomiting can be reduced when taken with food and respond extremely well to ondansetron and other antiemetics and should not be the reason to withhold oseltamivir when indicated.18,30Neuropsychiatric events are also an area of a concern and were added to the oseltamivir label after case reports of such events were reported (often after a single dose of oseltamivir), mainly out of Japan.12 Early evaluations of these events used a self-controlled case series design, which cannot account for underlying influenza infection.43 It is now well established that the influenza virus can precipitate neurologic complications, including acute necrotizing encephalopathy with high mortality.44,45 These complications include a wide spectrum of neurologic events, from seizures or transient encephalopathy lasting a few hours to fulminant acute necrotizing encephalopathy with progression from uncomplicated febrile upper respiratory illness to death within 24 hours.44,45 Recently, one of us (JA) performed a retrospective cohort study of 692 295 children with Medicaid insurance in the state of Tennessee and found that oseltamivir treatment was associated with a 47% reduction in neuropsychiatric events resulting in hospitalization (incidence rate ratio 0.53; 95% CI 0.33–0.88). These findings were in line with other well controlled studies using different data sources and study designs showing that influenza itself is associated with neuropsychiatric events and that oseltamivir use reduces this complication.12,46–52Although oseltamivir is the most prescribed antiviral, there is slow but growing use of baloxavir in both children and adults. Baloxavir is a cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitor that is FDA approved for early treatment of uncomplicated influenza in those aged at least 5 years that is as or more effective than oseltamivir in shortening duration of influenza symptoms.31,32 Baloxavir has some therapeutic advantages over oseltamivir, including a greater and more rapid reduction in viral load, reduced household influenza transmission, single-dose administration, better efficacy for influenza B strains, and better palatability.31,32,53–58 Some studies suggest that baloxavir may have a greater impact on influenza complications and hospitalization than oseltamivir33,59,60 and does not have vomiting or neuropsychiatric events listed on the label. Most of the antiviral prescribing in the Huang study was for oseltamivir, which included only 3 baloxavir users. Although baloxavir has been shown to be cost-effective,53 it is more expensive than oseltamivir and not always covered by Medicaid or insurance, likely limiting its widespread use.With greater public hesitancy regarding vaccines, declining seasonal influenza vaccination rates, and recent influenza seasons with record pediatric deaths and hospitalizations, providers should strongly consider the use of antivirals in high-risk and hospitalized patients.44,61,62 Many studies support the CDC, AAP, and IDSA recommendations on the use of oseltamivir and other influenza antivirals and demonstrate they are cost-effective, especially in high-risk individuals53,63–65 Outside of hospitalization, benefits of antivirals also include reduced household transmission of influenza, decreased influenza complications, and faster return to school for patients and work for parents.2,12,24,25,31–33,53–58,66–70 The CDC, AAP, IDSA and influenza experts all recommend prompt antiviral treatment of influenza as soon as possible after symptom onset in persons who are at increased risk of influenza complications, including children aged under 2 years and those with high-risk co-morbidities. The time has come for antivirals to be used in children with influenza.
